subject: Requesting ownership exceptions + ops playbook for Order Form
messages:
From: Sarah Merchant <sarah.merchant@brightwave.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Patricia Liu <patricia.liu@external-legal.com>, contracts@brightwave.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form - ownership carveout request

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the walk-through earlier. Our legal team reviewed the latest Order Form and asked for two narrow exceptions we'd like to discuss before procurement signs off:

1) Output ownership: BrightWave is requesting that for any outputs generated using their customer data, BrightWave retain title to the outputs for productization purposes (i.e., ability to sell or sublicense derivative products built from those outputs).
2) Training / feedback license: BrightWave wants an explicit opt-out from allowing Redwood to use their data, outputs, or feedback to further train models or to incorporate into model improvements.

I attached a short draft of suggested contract language (BrightWave-requested-clause.docx). Their reasoning is mostly regulatory and downstream IP monetization — they need to ensure they can package model-derived features into their SaaS.

Can your team tell me whether these carveouts are feasible and what the operational constraints would be? If feasible, we need:
- precise clause language we can include in the Order Form / Schedule
- a short ops playbook (who to notify internally when a customer elects the opt-out, data retention flow, telemetry exceptions)
- expected lead time for implementation/QA

Appreciate a quick turn — procurement would like to hit e-sign this week if possible.

Best,
Sarah Merchant
Head of Partnerships
BrightWave Inc.

Attachment: BrightWave-requested-clause.docx
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: sarah.merchant@brightwave.com, patricia.liu@external-legal.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form - ownership carveout request

Laura / Ben / Monica —

Forwarding BrightWave's ask. Short summary below and proposed approach.

Summary of asks (from Sarah):
- BrightWave wants title to outputs derived from their customer data; they want to productize derivatives.
- They want an explicit opt-out so Redwood will not use their data/outputs/feedback to train or improve models.

My read: this is higher-risk on the training side but plausible as a paid feature (training opt-out + additional controls). Ownership/title to outputs is more nuanced — we generally grant customers broad rights to use outputs, but blanket transfer of "title" could conflict with our model IP and productization policy.

Proposed compromise (to present to BrightWave):
- Output license: Grant BrightWave a perpetual, worldwide, sublicensable license to use, reproduce, and distribute outputs for their products, including the right to create derivative works, but reserve Redwood's right to use anonymized telemetry and aggregated usage metrics. Do NOT assign model weights or underlying model IP.
- Training opt-out: Offer a paid opt-out: Redwood will not use customer-provided content, outputs, or customer feedback for model training or fine-tuning for general models. Exceptions: safety signals and security incident data (we need those). We will record the opt-out election on the account and implement a data-handling flow.

Operational asks if we proceed:
- Monica: can you outline a minimal ops playbook so we can commit a lead time to BrightWave? Think: account flag, data retention deletion timelines, telemetry scoping, contract metadata.
- Ben: commercial markup for this feature (one-time or annual).
- Laura: legal to draft redline language consistent with our standard MSA + order form patterns. If we can get a redline today, I can get it to BrightWave for review.

I'm attaching a quick redline of the Order Form with placeholders (Redwood-OrderForm-v3-redline.pdf).

We should aim to give BrightWave a clear yes/no and an implementation timeline within 48 hours.

Thanks —
Grace
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood-OrderForm-v3-redline.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, ben.carter@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: sarah.merchant@brightwave.com, patricia.liu@external-legal.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 18:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form - ownership carveout request

Hi team — quick legal read and guidance.

High-level: we can draft language that materially satisfies BrightWave while protecting Redwood's core IP and ability to operate. Key guardrails: 
- We will NOT assign our model weights or underlying model IP. Any license we grant must be expressly limited to customer outputs.
- "Title" language is tricky; substitute with a "perpetual, worldwide, sublicensable license to exploit outputs" clause plus an affirmative statement that Redwood retains rights in the model and derived software components.
- For the training opt-out, we can offer an account-level opt-out that prevents use of customer data for model training and fine-tuning of Redwood's general models. We need to carve out safety/security uses and aggregated telemetry required for metricing/SLA enforcement.

Redline suggestions (excerpt):
- "Customer Outputs License": "Subject to payment, Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable license to use, reproduce, modify and distribute Outputs for Customer's internal business purposes and productization. Redwood expressly retains ownership of the underlying model, model weights, training data, and improvements thereto."
- "Training Opt-Out": "If Customer elects the Training Opt-Out in the Order Form, Redwood will not use Customer Data, Outputs, or Customer Feedback to train or improve Redwood's general-purpose models. Redwood may continue to process such data for performance, security, and billing purposes. This opt-out will be reflected as an account flag and is effective within 5 business days of Order Form execution."

Operational/implementation items I recommend we include in the ops playbook:
- Account flagging mechanism in Console (indicate opt-out + effective date)
- Data retention/deletion SLA (e.g., 30 days to remove queued training artifacts; 90 days to purge telemetry used for model improvement pipelines)
- Security/safety exception process (how incidents are routed to legal/SRE)
- Audit trail / attestation for customers who request proof of opt-out handling

I've attached a short note with the redline excerpts and recommended timelines (legal_summary_training_optout.txt). If Ben/Grace want, we can send the proposed language to BrightWave as-is and highlight non-negotiables.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: legal_summary_training_optout.txt
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: sarah.merchant@brightwave.com, contracts@brightwave.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 20:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form - ownership carveout request

Perfect — thanks Laura and Grace. From a commercial standpoint:

- We're OK to offer the Training Opt-Out as a paid add-on. Proposal: $35k annual for the account-level opt-out + $6k onboarding/ops set-up fee (covers console flagging + audit).
- Output license: we'll accept the "perpetual sublicensable license" draft Laura proposed. We should add a short clause that prohibits BrightWave from sublicensing the outputs to create competing hosted LLM services that replicate Redwood's product (narrow non-compete carveout).

Next steps:
- Grace/Laura: please send the redlined Order Form (use Laura's wording) back to BrightWave for acceptance.
- Monica: please draft the ops playbook stub (account flagging, 30/90 day deletion windows, exception workflow) and drop into the Google doc linked below. I'll include the commercial pricing in the HubSpot deal.

I'll mark the HubSpot deal as "Procurement in review" and coordinate signatures once we have the redline agreed. Sarah — happy to jump on a 15-min call if you want to walk the team through any of this.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
